concepts.def: 0 ≤ P(A) ≤ 1; P(Ω) = 1; mutually exclusive events: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B).
P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B)/P(B). Probability of A given B has occurred.
Events A, B independent ⟺ P(A ∩ B) = P(A) · P(B). Equivalently, P(A|B) = P(A).
Branches show sequential outcomes with conditional probabilities. Multiply along branches; add at endpoints.
Visualise sets and intersections. Useful for P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B).
P(A|B) = P(B|A) · P(A) / P(B). Updates beliefs given new evidence. Used in medical testing, spam filtering.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Probability — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Probability brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Probability.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
